This arrived about an hour ago, and I have to admit that I am pretty jazzed about this inexpensive quartz watch.

For a mere $220, Dan Henry's model 1939 delivers quite an impressive package. As you can see from the photos, it comes in a plastic tube container. While the plastic is unremarkable, its contents most certainly are.

This watch comes with a canvas and leather 3-watch roll, an unexpectedly nice leather strap, as well as a black military-grade NATO.

Seeing as how I just got the thing, I can only give immediate impressions, but they are all positive. The lovely black, subtly textured dial is home to what appears (to the naked eye, at least, I'll be getting my loupe out later) to be flawless raised glossy features as well as applied Arabic numbers/markers. The subdials are embellished with a concentric circles design which I find quite pleasing. Oh, and on that note, the seconds subdial's hand actually hits the tic-marks perfectly.

The 1939 is powered by the Miyota 6S21, which I am actually grateful for. Were this piece mechanical (good mechanical), no way could I afford it. I actually have a sibling of this movement running my CASIO Speedmasterum Ripofficus and it has yet to let me down.

The features of the watch are as follows:

  • Telemeter: it measures the distance travelled by a sound wave, allowing to know how far away a bomb just exploded; from the difference between the light and sound of the same phenomenon.

  • Tachometer: it calculates the average speed according to the distance travelled.

  • Pulsometer: it counts your heartbeats.

  • It also is pretty handy at telling you what time it is.

The crystal is domed and comprised of sapphire-coated mineral. I've never had one of these before and am curious as to how it will stand-up to the rigors of time. Materials be damned, this is one gorgeous dome.

I must confess that when I saw this watch online last week, I knew that I absolutely had to have it. This freakin' thing checks-off boxes I didn't even know I had. The design as a whole really speaks to me, and I am in no way ashamed to say that it is absolutely one of the most beautiful wristwatches that I have ever seen.

If this piece is half-as durable as it is beautiful, this baby is gonna dominate my wrist time-wise.

As if you couldn't tell, I am mighty pleased with this purchase and I adore the damn thing already.

Thank you for your time.
